name: Welsh Rarebit
description: Welsh rarebit is genuinely not cheese on toast, despite how it's often described - real technique cooks a real savory cheese sauce separately first, built on a roux with ale, mustard, and Worcestershire sauce, then pours it over toast and broils until golden. The dish's real name is a satirical joke from 1725, originally 'Welsh rabbit', implying cheese was the poor man's meat since Welsh peasants of the time genuinely couldn't afford real rabbit or meat.

steps_detailed: Melt the butter in a small saucepan, whisk in the flour, and cook 1 minute.
Add the ale, mustard, and Worcestershire sauce, stirring constantly over low heat.
Add the cheese gradually, melting it in slowly over low heat - real technique keeps this gentle, never letting it overheat or the sauce can split.
Pour the sauce generously over the toasted bread.
Broil 2-3 minutes until golden and bubbling.

name: Welsh Bara Brith
description: Bara brith, meaning 'speckled bread' in Welsh, genuinely depends on real technique of soaking the dried fruit overnight in strong black tea before baking - this real soak is what deepens the fruit's flavor and gives the finished loaf its distinctive moist, speckled crumb.

ingredients_full.ingredient: Beverages, tea, black, brewed, prepared with tap water

steps_detailed: Soak the raisins in the hot strong tea overnight - real technique depends on this real, long soak, not a quick dip.
The next day, mix the flour, sugar, baking powder, and allspice with the egg and the soaked fruit along with its soaking liquid.
Pour into a loaf pan and bake at 325F (165C) for 55-60 minutes until a skewer comes out clean.
Slice thick and serve with butter.

name: Welsh Cawl
description: Cawl, Wales' real national dish, is a slow-cooked lamb, leek, and root vegetable broth, real technique building real depth from a long, patient simmer rather than a quick cook.
steps_detailed: Brown the lamb, 8-9 minutes.
Add the rutabaga, carrot, and enough water to cover, and simmer 1-1.5 hours, until the lamb is genuinely tender.
Add the potato and leeks, and simmer 20-22 minutes more until everything is tender.

name: Welsh Cakes
description: Welsh cakes, real griddle-cooked, currant-studded cakes, are a beloved teatime treat, real technique cooking them on a dry griddle or bakestone, never in the oven.
steps_detailed: Mix the flour and butter into coarse crumbs, then work in the sugar, raisins, allspice, and egg into a firm dough.
Roll out and cut into rounds.
Cook on a dry, hot griddle or skillet, 2-3 minutes per side, until golden - real Welsh cakes are never baked in the oven.

name: Welsh Leek Soup (Cawl Cennin)
description: Cawl cennin, a real leek and potato soup, celebrates the leek, one of Wales' national symbols, real technique cooking the leeks gently so they stay sweet rather than bitter.
steps_detailed: Cook the leeks in the butter over low heat, 6-8 minutes, gently so they don't brown or turn bitter.
Add the potato and broth, and simmer 18-20 minutes until tender.
Blend until smooth, or leave chunky if preferred.

description: Grilled salmon, seasoned simply with butter and herbs, reflects Wales' rich coastal and river fishing tradition.
steps_detailed: Rub the salmon with the butter and lemon juice, and let sit 10 minutes.
Grill or broil, 4-5 minutes per side, until just cooked through.
